name: Female Adnexal Tumor of Probable Wolffian Origin

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for FATWO

criteria.description: Presence of tubular, sieve-like, or retiform architectural patterns on histology consistent with Wolffian origin
Positive immunostaining for markers such as inhibin, calretinin, and cytokeratin with negative epithelial markers
Tumor localized to female adnexal structures (broad ligament, fallopian tube, or ovary) without evidence of other primary tumors
Absence of mutations typical for other adnexal tumors (e.g., absence of FOXL2 mutation seen in granulosa cell tumors)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of characteristic architecture plus positive immunohistochemical profile and tumor localization in female adnexa
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other sex cord-stromal and epithelial tumors.

laboratory: Possible mild hypercalcemia in rare cases
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing well-circumscribed adnexal mass
CT scan may reveal solid or cystic adnexal lesion without ascites
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for inhibin, calretinin, cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: FOXL2 mutation present in granulosa cell tumor
Different immunohistochemical profile (positive for FOXL2, negative for Wolffian markers)
Distinct histology with Sertoli and Leydig cell components

redFlags: Signs of metastatic disease such as lymphadenopathy or ascites
